messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: high 5xx rate for /v1/generate in eu-west (region=europe-west1, az=europe-west1-b). Impact: ~20% error rate, elevated latency. Incident channel opened. @eve_oncall paging.

pagerduty: @eve_oncall — on-call acknowledged (priority: P1).

eve_oncall: I'm on it. quick check: is this a client-side surge or routing? any recent deploys to eu-west?

alice_sre: No deploys in the last hour from infra teams. I'm pulling LB/egress metrics now.

bob_net: Seeing cross-region egress spike from eu-west1-b to eu-central backends. Some flows are being routed to eu-central despite region-pin=eu-west being set.

frank_enginfra: Confirmed: routing policy service shows a stale cache entry for route group "eu-west-pref" on proxies in europe-west1-b. TTLs look normal but pins are mismatched between control-plane and edge.

alice_sre: Digging into agent logs on a representative host:
```
2024-04-05T09:10:12Z route-manager INFO apply: pin=eu-west region=eu-west agent_state=APPLIED
2024-04-05T09:11:03Z route-manager WARN sync: desired_pin=eu-west actual_pin=eu-central
2024-04-05T09:11:04Z net-proxy ERROR forward: upstream_unavailable, falling back
```

bob_net: I ran `dig +short @8.8.8.8 route.eu.redwood.net` and got both eu-west and eu-central CNAMEs; cache timestamps show recent updates. Looks like some proxies are honoring new steering weights incorrectly (weight flip).

gina_cs: Any customer-facing impact? Support dashboard shows several active errors for customers in EU with churn of streaming responses. CS is getting escalating tickets.

dave_support: We have a handful of customers reporting truncated streams and 5xx on retries. ETA to mitigate? Customers are asking for a scope and ETA.

eve_oncall: Triage summary: cross-region routing policy misapplication causing failover to eu-central from eu-west AZ b, increasing latency and 5xx. Likely root: inconsistent pin propagation / control-plane race after a recent policy push. Plan: (1) stop automatic failover by writing temporary override pin on affected proxies; (2) flush downstream proxy caches; (3) if needed, rollback last routing policy change. Need network + infra to coordinate.

bob_net: I'll push a temporary `pin-override=eu-west` to the proxy fleet in europe-west1-b only (no-global) and set it to sticky with TTL=300s. Command: `rbctl route override --region eu-west --az b --pin eu-west --ttl 300 --reason "incident 1712349999 pin-override"`

frank_enginfra: I'll coordinate the rollout. Starting canary to 5 hosts and watching error rate.

alice_sre: Canary metrics: error rate on canary hosts drops from 18% -> 1.5% within 30s after override. Latency also normalizes. Good signal.

eve_oncall: proceed to 100% in AZ b only. frank, confirm once full rollout done. Also we should add a short-term health-check override to prevent autoscaling from killing canary hosts.

frank_enginfra: Rollout to eu-west1-b completed at 09:24:12Z. Verified via `rbctl status`:
```
host-045 pinned eu-west
host-046 pinned eu-west
host-047 pinned eu-west
```
Edge error-rate for the AZ down from 21% -> 2%.

bob_net: Flushed proxy DNS cache and restarted route-agent on 12 hosts. Verified control-plane now reports desired_pin==actual_pin across eu-west1-b.

alice_sre: Confirming customer impact: 95th latency back to baseline, errors down to ~1.8% global, eu-west at 2.1%.

gina_cs: Notifying affected customers: CS will message a short note: "We've mitigated a routing incident impacting EU traffic; we're monitoring and will follow up with a root cause within the postmortem."

carol_prod: Was there a policy change that triggered the propagation race? Need to know if rollout tooling allowed partial application.

bob_net: Looks like a policy push 09:05Z modified steering weights for a canary rollout; control-plane issued concurrent updates which created a transient split-brain in the route cache for az b. The route-agent's reconcile loop uses eventual consistency and our last-write-wins logic ended up causing flip-flop.

eve_oncall: Immediate mitigation done. Next steps: (A) keep pin-override until next maintenance window (B) create a safety check in rollout tool to detect concurrent policy edits to the same route group (C) add a monitoring alert for pin divergence (control-plane vs agent) with >=2 hosts in an AZ disagreeing. Assign owners.

frank_enginfra: I'll own A and help schedule window to remove override.

bob_net: I'll own B, plan to add a guard in the operator to lock route groups during rollout.

alice_sre: I'll own C and create the alert query; will draft dashboard and initial threshold.

dave_support: CS and Support will prepare a short customer-facing incident note and a follow-up with timeline once we have RCA.

gina_cs: Noted. Sending out initial customer messages now.

eve_oncall: Handoff: @frank_enginfra will be primary for the next 4 hours to manage the override and rollback schedule. I'll remain available for triage if we see regressions. If anything spikes above 5% error rate again, re-pager.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 09:40Z — mitigation confirmed.

alice_sre: Captured logs and sample traces for postmortem. Saving session IDs: trace-zz1, trace-zz2.

bob_net: Quick note: we also saw some curious cache TTL jitter on route-agent causing skewed apply times (milliseconds) — I'll instrument histograms.

eve_oncall: Thanks team. I'll file the incident ticket and schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow. Closing active mitigation thread, leaving follow-up tasks in the incident tracker.

gina_cs: Customer messages queued. No new escalations as of 09:50Z.

carol_prod: Please include a pointer to the exact policy diff in the postmortem (policy id: rpg-2024-04-05-221).

frank_enginfra: Acknowledged. We'll coordinate removal of pin-override during maintenance window on 2024-04-06 02:00Z UTC if no further regressions.

dave_support: Thanks everyone.

eve_oncall: Closing slack thread, moving notes to incident tracker. Good work. :thumbsup:
